### Called to Carry
Author: Jill Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-women/called-to-carry-one-year-devotions-for-women-january-20.html
Passage: Numbers 4:15
Points:
- God gave Aaron and the priests the task of preparing the holy furnishings, while the Kohathites were assigned the duty of carrying them.
- Discontentment arose two generations later when Korah rebelled, desiring visible leadership rather than his assigned role.
- Division occurs when people seek their own status rather than God's calling, whereas contentment comes from accepting one's given place.
- No service given by God is insignificant, regardless of how ordinary or heavy the task may seem.
- Believers assigned supportive roles should carry out their ministry with joy and purpose.

### Worship Leaders as Kohathites: Called to Serve in Most Holy Things
Author: Zac Hicks
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/worship-leaders-as-kohathites-called-to-serve-in-most-holy-things/
Passage: Numbers 4:1-4, 17-20
Points:
- God gave the Kohathites strict instructions and solemn warnings regarding the transport of the most sacred tabernacle furnishings.
- Worship leaders and facilitators share an analogous calling today, charged with stewarding sacred elements of public worship.
- Gathered worship should never become casual or careless, because God's holiness remains majestic and weighty.
- Jesus served as the flawless representative who removed judgment and made bold access to God possible.
- Ministry leaders should maintain reverence for their high calling while resting in Christ as their covering.
